---
name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: AyushRajSinghParihar
  source: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines
---

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support or product-feasibility decisions, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. For an exact component, technology, or unfamiliar term, search the
   [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md). It links directly to local
   topic procedures. Enter the procedure before its supporting reference. Do not
   load the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Platform: iOS/macOS. Current palette uses white backgrounds, light gray body text and red versus green dots as the only route-status meaning. Selected route is indicated by a slightly darker red. Exact color values are not provided.

name: apple-hig-foundations
description: Use when designing or reviewing Apple-platform visual hierarchy, accessibility, typography, color, Liquid Glass, layout, icons, imagery, motion, privacy, inclusion, localization, or spatial interfaces.

# Apple HIG: Perception, meaning and adaptable presentation

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the actual barrier or design decision: readability, visual hierarchy, imagery meaning, movement, locale, privacy or spatial placement. Choose the corresponding topic procedure rather than loading every foundation.
2. For text access, combine Typography with Accessibility only where size, reflow or reading alternatives matter. Use VoiceOver when grouping, semantics or navigation needs a procedure of its own.
3. For color/material decisions, separate content hierarchy from controls and evaluate the actual appearance/background/settings context. Preserve semantic meaning when appearance changes.
4. Deliver prioritized evidence-backed corrections or a concrete presentation specification. Distinguish inspected contrast/layout evidence from runtime and assistive-technology checks still needed.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification
or patch. Load related topics only when the chosen procedure calls for them.

- [Accessibility](.topics/apple-hig-accessibility/SKILL.md)
- [App icons](.topics/apple-hig-app-icons/SKILL.md)
- [Branding](.topics/apple-hig-branding/SKILL.md)

- [Immersive experiences](.topics/apple-hig-immersive-experiences/SKILL.md)

- [Typography](.topics/apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md)
- [Writing](.topics/apple-hig-writing/SKILL.md)

## Completion evidence

Report the concrete decisions or changes, their source support, and which checks
passed, failed or were not executed. A source citation or a list of links is not
the requested work product. Retain platform exceptions and unresolved source
conflicts; the absence of a platform subsection does not establish support.

name: apple-hig-color
description: Use when choosing or reviewing Apple-platform color semantics, custom palettes, contrast, Liquid Glass tint, color profiles, or cross-appearance color behavior.
---

# Assign color by meaning and viewing context

Read [Color](../../references/color.md). Inspect the actual foreground/background pairs, semantic roles, assets, appearances, and supported platforms. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Record unknown rendered colors instead of inventing contrast measurements. Preserve the current stack while expressing the requested palette or implementation change.

Classify each color as content, interactive accent, state, text, separator, or background hierarchy. Reuse semantic system roles where they fit; do not borrow a separator color for text or copy dated RGB swatches into production constants. Keep meanings consistent and pair important color distinctions with words/shapes/icons.

For custom colors, specify light/dark and increased-contrast variants, including local glass appearances even in a single-appearance app. Inspect resting and scrolled compositions against real underlying content. On glass, keep ordinary labels/symbols monochrome and tint sparingly for primary action or important status; prefer a colored primary-button background to colored button text.

Branch by context: honor user accents on Mac, use motion/scale as well as color for TV focus, check visionOS glass against varied surroundings without isolated glaring elements in darkness, and keep Watch complications useful in a single-color tint. For image fidelity, preserve embedded profiles and choose sRGB or appropriate wide-gamut assets based on actual display tests; do not assume two close P3 colors survive sRGB conversion.

**Before → decision → after:** A finance graph uses red/green lines and the same green for inactive labels and a Buy button. Decision: distinguish data from interactivity and retain meaning without hue. After, named/dashed series accompany color, neutral semantic labels describe values, and one accent marks the actionable control, with appearance-specific tested variants.

Deliver a role-to-color mapping plus corrected artifact. Fail if a noninteractive element resembles a link, a state disappears without color, or measured text/icon contrast falls short of the applicable guide. Report calculator inputs/results; hardware, ambient-light, TV-brand, or spatial-background claims require actual checks.

Continue with [Dark Mode](../apple-hig-dark-mode/SKILL.md) for appearance transitions, [Materials](../apple-hig-materials/SKILL.md) for glass surfaces, or [Accessibility](../apple-hig-accessibility/SKILL.md) for broader sensory access.

---
name: apple-hig-dark-mode
description: Use when designing, reviewing, or adapting light and dark appearances, automatic appearance transitions, semantic surfaces, or mode-specific assets on supported Apple platforms.
---

# Adapt the hierarchy to appearance

Read [Dark Mode](../../references/dark-mode.md). Inspect supported platforms, semantic colors, elevated surfaces, asset variants, and live-switch behavior. This guide covers iOS/iPadOS/macOS/tvOS and marks visionOS/watchOS unsupported; do not impose its appearance model on those platforms. Choose design, review, or adaptation mode and distinguish rendered evidence from a proposed palette.

Start from system appearance rather than duplicating it with an app-only switch. If a permanently dark media context is proposed, establish the reason; do not turn that exception into a default for ordinary tasks. Define what happens when appearance changes while a sheet, selection, or text field is active.

Replace literal light/dark fills with semantic surface/text roles or matched custom color sets. Preserve base-versus-elevated distinction on iOS/iPadOS rather than mechanically inverting every value. Check custom glyph outlines and full-color artwork in both modes: reuse an asset if it works, otherwise provide variants under one identity. Reduce a bright image's harsh glow only when necessary without distorting its content.

Test Increase Contrast and Reduce Transparency independently and together. Use the guide's contrast targets for this scope; record actual color pairs and measurements. For Mac desktop tinting, a neutral custom surface may share subtle transparency, but colored states should not change meaning as wallpaper moves behind them.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a notes app inverts its white page to black but leaves fixed gray placeholder text and a white imported diagram. Decision: hierarchy and readable content must adapt together. After, system text/surface roles define the editor, elevated panels remain distinguishable, and a mode-appropriate diagram treatment avoids a glaring rectangle while preserving information.

Deliver corrected appearance tokens/assets or a review with precise failing pairs. Fail if runtime switching leaves a light-only element, an elevated panel merges into its parent, or accessibility settings reduce readability. A static palette cannot verify native vibrancy or desktop tinting; list those checks as pending.

Use [Color](../apple-hig-color/SKILL.md) for semantic role selection and [Images](../apple-hig-images/SKILL.md) when the problem lies in asset production.

---
name: apple-hig-accessibility
description: Use when designing, reviewing, or adapting Apple-platform interfaces for text enlargement, sensory access, assistive input, motor access, cognitive needs, or accessibility preferences.
---

# Make the task accessible

Read [Accessibility guidance](../../references/accessibility.md) before applying platform values. This procedure turns that guidance into task-level changes; its artifact format and prioritization are application engineering advice, not additional Apple requirements.

## Establish what can be evaluated

Identify the supported platform, the person's task from entry to completion, and whether the request is design, review, or adaptation. Inspect the supplied screens, content, interaction description, semantics, or implementation. Record which evidence exists: a screenshot can establish visible labels and geometry, but cannot establish spoken names, focus order, alternative activation, or preference behavior. Continue using explicit assumptions when the platform or behavior is missing; ask only when the choice changes the requested result.

For a review, connect each finding to an observed barrier and its consequence for that task. Separate untested behavior needing verification from confirmed defects. For a design or adaptation, change the authorized artifact itself: a revised screen specification, interaction contract, or implementation. A general accessibility checklist alone is not the deliverable.

## Remove the barriers that the task contains

Trace the task without assuming sight, hearing, fine motor control, speech, or fast responses. Select the applicable branches:

- **Reading and visual distinctions:** Preserve content and available actions when text enlarges. Use the guide's platform-specific text defaults and minima; its resizing guidance is at least 200%, with 140% stated for watchOS. Reflow or expose another usable arrangement rather than clipping essential labels. Pair color distinctions with text, shape, or symbols. Evaluate actual foreground/background combinations in light and dark appearances; use a contrast calculator and preserve the guide's stated contrast-table scope instead of claiming that its values alone establish conformance. If the default scheme falls short, specify the Increase Contrast treatment.
- **Information carried by sound or imagery:** Identify what information would disappear when sound or sight is unavailable. Choose captions for synchronized audible events, subtitles for dialogue translation, audio description for visual events, or transcripts for a complete text account according to the content. Specify descriptions for meaningful interface/content imagery and omit redundant decoration. Pair essential sound feedback with a perceivable visual or appropriate haptic equivalent.
- **Manipulation and navigation:** Distinguish visible control size from its actual activation area and separation. Use the guide's platform default as the starting point; its smaller minimum is not a blanket recommendation for dense controls. Replace essential complex or repeated gestures with a labeled onscreen action. Make the complete task navigable and activatable with the supported keyboard and assistive input paths; speech must not be necessary. Preserve system accessibility shortcuts. For custom controls, specify names, roles, values, states, and task order rather than assuming their appearance supplies semantics.
- **Time, motion, and comprehension:** Give people time to read and act; prefer explicit dismissal when transient content requires attention. If motion is present, define a Reduce Motion version that retains state and meaning while reducing automatic movement, bounce, zoom, or depth changes. If media autoplays, provide playback control and consider a global preference; honor Dim Flashing Lights where applicable. Keep the task's navigation and wording consistent rather than adding instructional clutter.

Apply the relevant platform condition. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks with one interaction per screen and the source's two confirmations for difficult-to-reverse actions in that mode. For visionOS, keep controls in comfortable view, avoid head-locked content and repeated large gestures, and accommodate hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. These conditions do not apply automatically to every platform.

## Deliver and check the result

Return the revised artifact or evidence-based review, including the barrier, the concrete change, and its acceptance check. State which platform/preferences were considered and which claims remain unverified. Prioritize blockers to completing the task over cosmetic refinements.

Exercise each selected alternative along the same entry-to-completion path. Fail the check if essential content or actions disappear at the specified text scale, information remains available through only one sense, a required gesture has no equivalent, focus cannot reach/activate a necessary control, or a requested motion accommodation removes meaning. Measure contrast and activation geometry when the evidence permits; report missing measurements rather than inventing them. Use Accessibility Inspector and relevant VoiceOver, Switch Control, Full Keyboard Access, AssistiveTouch, or Pointer Control tests on supported Apple environments. Static inspection or a Linux run cannot establish those runtime results, Apple-device comfort, or App Store Accessibility Nutrition Label eligibility.

## Worked transformation

**Before:** An iPad astronomy log marks observation quality only with green/red dots, announces saving with a chime, and exposes Delete only by a two-finger gesture.

**Decision:** Logging must remain understandable without color or sound and operable without that gesture. Retain compact rows while making status and actions explicit.

**After:** Each row reads “Clear” or “Clouded” alongside its symbol; saving exposes a persistent “Saved” state; a labeled row action opens Delete. The screen specification includes expanded-text reflow, semantic row status, and keyboard/assistive activation acceptance checks. These are proposed changes until the actual implementation passes those checks; the specification does not claim VoiceOver was tested.

## Continue only where needed

For detailed spoken structure and rotor navigation, use [VoiceOver](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-voiceover/SKILL.md). For text reflow/type choices use [Typography](../apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md); for a motion accommodation use [Motion](../apple-hig-motion/SKILL.md). If spatial comfort dominates the task, use [Spatial layout](../apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md). Keep the task's accessibility acceptance checks when handing off.

# Color Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/color) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. ## Contents - [Best practices](#Best-practices) - [Inclusive color](#Inclusive-color) - [System colors](#System-colors) - [Liquid Glass color](#Liquid-Glass-color) - [Color management](#Color-management) - [Platform considerations](#Platform-considerations) - [Specifications](#Specifications) - [Resources](#Resources) - [Change log](#Change-log) Use color to clarify hierarchy, state, continuity, and identity. Prefer system colors when their semantics fit: they adapt to appearance, vibrancy, and accessibility preferences. ## Best practices Keep each color’s meaning consistent; an interactive tint should not also decorate inert text. Provide light, dark, and increased-contrast variants for custom colors, including both appearances in a single-appearance app because Liquid Glass adapts locally. Test outdoors, in dim rooms, on different hardware and display profiles, and against visionOS physical backgrounds. True Tone changes white point on supported phones/tablets/Macs; media, reading, and game apps can specify white-point adaptivity. Test several HD/4K TV brands. Account for nearby artwork and translucent surfaces when choosing colors. Prefer a system color picker so people get familiar selection and shared saved colors. ## Inclusive color Pair essential color signals with words, shapes, or glyphs. Check text/icon contrast and combinations that can be hard to distinguish. Consider cultural meanings rather than assuming colors convey universal emotions or warnings. ## System colors Use APIs rather than copying numeric system values, which can change by release and environment. Dynamic semantic colors describe purpose, such as label, separator, link, or hierarchical background. Preserve those meanings rather than borrowing separator colors for text or label colors for fills. ## Liquid Glass color Clear glass derives its appearance from the content behind it. Small bars can switch between light and dark with underlying content; labels and symbols normally remain monochrome. Larger surfaces such as sidebars become more opaque to preserve readability. Use tinted glass sparingly for important status or a primary action. To emphasize a primary button, color its background rather than its text or symbol, and avoid coloring several control backgrounds. Over colorful content, prefer monochrome bars or an accent that contrasts clearly; a brand accent works more readily against monochrome content. Check resting and initial layouts for overlap between similarly colored content and controls, not only intermediate scroll states. ## Color management A color model describes components such as RGB/CMYK; a color space defines their gamut, and an embedded profile maps numeric values to actual colors. Embed profiles in images; sRGB is broadly reliable. On a wide-color display, Display P3 can improve photo/video fidelity and visual differentiation. The source recommends Display P3 PNG with 16 bits per channel where appropriate. P3 imagery usually converts well to sRGB, but close colors or gradients can merge or clip; provide color-space-specific asset variants when testing exposes problems. ## Platform considerations ### iOS, iPadOS Use grouped backgrounds for grouped tables, otherwise the ordinary system background family. In each family, primary is the overall view, secondary groups within it, and tertiary groups within secondary content. |Role|UIKit API| |---|---| |Primary through quaternary labels|`label`, `secondaryLabel`, `tertiaryLabel`, `quaternaryLabel`| |Placeholder strings|`placeholderText`| |Translucent divider|`separator`| |Opaque divider|`opaqueSeparator`| |Linked text|`link`| |Ordinary backgrounds, levels 1–3|`systemBackground`, `secondarySystemBackground`, `tertiarySystemBackground`| |Grouped backgrounds, levels 1–3|`systemGroupedBackground`, `secondarySystemGroupedBackground`, `tertiarySystemGroupedBackground`| ### macOS Choose NSColor semantic APIs by the actual role, available in the standard Color panel’s Developer palette. |Role|NSColor API| |---|---| |Text on selection in table/list|`alternateSelectedControlTextColor`| |Alternating rows/columns|`alternatingContentBackgroundColors`| |User accent|`controlAccentColor`| |Browser/table background|`controlBackgroundColor`| |Control surface / enabled text|`controlColor`, `controlTextColor`| |System tint / disabled text|`currentControlTint`, `disabledControlTextColor`| |Find indicator / grid lines|`findHighlightColor`, `gridColor`| |Table header / virtual illumination|`headerTextColor`, `highlightColor`| |Keyboard focus ring|`keyboardFocusIndicatorColor`| |Primary through quaternary label|`labelColor`, `secondaryLabelColor`, `tertiaryLabelColor`, `quaternaryLabelColor`| |Link / placeholder|`linkColor`, `placeholderTextColor`| |Selected content in key view|`selectedContentBackgroundColor`| |Selected control / its text|`selectedControlColor`, `selectedControlTextColor`| |Selected menu text|`selectedMenuItemTextColor`| |Text-selection fill / selected text|`selectedTextBackgroundColor`, `selectedTextColor`| |Divider / raised-object shadow|`separatorColor`, `shadowColor`| |Document background / document text|`textBackgroundColor`, `textColor`| |Behind document|`underPageBackgroundColor`| |Inactive selected content|`unemphasizedSelectedContentBackgroundColor`| |Inactive text-selection fill / text|`unemphasizedSelectedTextBackgroundColor`, `unemphasizedSelectedTextColor`| |Window surface / title-bar text|`windowBackgroundColor`, `windowFrameTextColor`| #### App accent colors Since macOS 11, an app accent can color buttons, selections, and sidebar icons when the user chooses multicolor. Another user-selected accent overrides it, except fixed-color sidebar icons whose specific colors carry meaning. ### tvOS Use a restrained palette related to the app logo while letting content lead. Show focus through scaling and responsive motion as well as color. ### visionOS Physical and virtual colors show through glass. Use color for important relationships or emphasis, preferably in bold text or large areas rather than thin text and tiny details. Balance brightness during immersion: avoid isolated bright, flashing, or moving objects against dark surroundings when eyes have adapted to darkness. ### watchOS Background color can convey context or supporting information, such as a ring’s category. Avoid long-lived full-screen colored backgrounds in workouts or playback. Graphic complications must also work in the wearer’s chosen single-color tinted mode. ## Specifications ### System colors The following dated design-reference values were recovered from the official JSON swatch descriptions in the 2026-10-25 snapshot. Each tuple is an 8-bit RGB triplet. Use the semantic APIs in production instead of hard-coding these values: system colors can change with releases and context. SwiftUI properties are shown below; visionOS uses default dark values. |Color/API|Light RGB|Dark RGB|High-contrast light RGB|High-contrast dark RGB| |---|---|---|---|---| |Red / `red`|255,56,60|255,66,69|233,21,45|255,97,101| |Orange / `orange`|255,141,40|255,146,48|197,83,0|255,160,86| |Yellow / `yellow`|255,204,0|255,214,0|161,106,0|254,223,67| |Green / `green`|52,199,89|48,209,88|0,137,50|74,217,104| |Mint / `mint`|0,200,179|0,218,195|0,133,117|84,223,203| |Teal / `teal`|0,195,208|0,210,224|0,129,152|59,221,236| |Cyan / `cyan`|0,192,232|60,211,254|0,126,174|109,217,255| |Blue / `blue`|0,136,255|0,145,255|30,110,244|92,184,255| |Indigo / `indigo`|97,85,245|109,124,255|86,74,222|167,170,255| |Purple / `purple`|203,48,224|219,52,242|176,47,194|234,141,255| |Pink / `pink`|255,45,85|255,55,95|231,18,77|255,138,196| |Brown / `brown`|172,127,94|183,138,102|149,109,81|219,166,121| ### iOS, iPadOS system gray colors UIKit supplies the six gray variants below. These are dated 2026-10-25 design-reference RGB values, not production constants. SwiftUI `Color.gray` corresponds to `systemGray`. |Color/API|Light RGB|Dark RGB|High-contrast light RGB|High-contrast dark RGB| |---|---|---|---|---| |Gray / `systemGray`|142,142,147|142,142,147|108,108,112|174,174,178| |Gray (2) / `systemGray2`|174,174,178|99,99,102|142,142,147|124,124,128| |Gray (3) / `systemGray3`|199,199,204|72,72,74|174,174,178|84,84,86| |Gray (4) / `systemGray4`|209,209,214|58,58,60|188,188,192|68,68,70| |Gray (5) / `systemGray5`|229,229,234|44,44,46|216,216,220|54,54,56| |Gray (6) / `systemGray6`|242,242,247|28,28,30|235,235,240|36,36,38| ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/color) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: December 16, 2025, June 9, 2025, February 2, 2024, September 12, 2023, June 21, 2023, June 5, 2023, December 19, 2022.

# Dark Mode Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/dark-mode) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Respect system light/dark appearance preferences on iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and tvOS. Dark Mode uses darker backgrounds and lighter foregrounds with purpose-specific contrast, rather than mechanically inverting every color. ## Best practices Avoid a separate app appearance switch that duplicates system settings. Handle automatic appearance changes while the app is running. Test both appearances with Increase Contrast and Reduce Transparency separately and together; increased contrast can expose unexpected low-contrast dark text. A permanently dark presentation is an uncommon exception for contexts such as immersive media where surrounding UI should recede. ## Dark Mode colors Choose semantic adaptive colors and asset-catalog Color Sets for custom bright/dim variants, rather than fixed values. Maintain at least 4.5:1 foreground/background contrast; aim for 7:1 with custom colors, especially small type. Slightly dim white-background images if they glow harshly in a dark interface. ### Icons and images Prefer SF Symbols with dynamic tint or vibrancy. # Transit disruption dashboard: revised interaction specification

## Scope and evidence

Design specification for iOS/macOS, independent of framework or Apple SDK. The task is to identify a route’s service status, select it, and read its disruption details across appearances. "'`interface.md` supplies only a prose description: white backgrounds, light gray body text, red/green dots as the sole status signal, and slightly darker red for selection. It supplies no exact colors, implementation, screenshots, route data, or control behavior.

Confirmed barriers in that description: status disappears without color discrimination; selection and disruption share a red encoding. Light gray body text is a contrast concern, not a measured failure. The route names and messages below are illustrative, not supplied service data.

## Decisions and source basis

1. Assign color by purpose: surface hierarchy, primary/secondary text, interaction, selection, and service status have separate tokens. Do not use separator colors for body text. Prefer a platform semantic resolver where available; otherwise use the explicit custom fallback below. Never copy numeric system swatches as production constants. [Color — System colors](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/color#System-colors).
2. Keep disruption red and normal service green as supplementary cues, with a persistent status phrase and distinct symbol. Unknown service is neutral and explicitly named. Status is information, not an error action or a link. No colored whole-row fill for disruption. [Color — Inclusive color](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/color#Inclusive-color), [Accessibility — Vision](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility#Vision).
3. Make selection independent of service status: selection background plus a neutral leading rule and the word “Selected.” Reserve a separate focus outline for keyboard focus. On macOS, honor the user’s accent for interactive focus and appropriate platform selection styling; never recolor service status to match the accent. [Color — macOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/color#macOS).
4. Follow system appearance and accessibility preferences; do not add an app-only appearance switch. Re-resolve every visible role on a preference change without losing selection, focus, detail content, or scroll position. Preserve iOS base/elevated surface hierarchy rather than simply inverting colors. [Dark Mode — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/dark-mode#Best-practices), [Dark Mode — iOS/iPadOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/dark-mode#iOS-iPadOS).
5. Use opaque content surfaces for this revision. This is a product choice that keeps status independent of wallpaper and content behind the dashboard. No glass is required. If a host adds translucent chrome later, resolve its local appearance separately, keep ordinary labels monochrome, and retest composited contrast; do not reuse a global light/dark assumption for glass. [Color — Liquid Glass color](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/color#Liquid-Glass-color), [Dark Mode — macOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/dark-mode#macOS).

## Semantic role contract

| Token | Use and platform mapping intent |
|---|---|
| `surface.base` | Dashboard background; ordinary system background on iOS, window background on macOS |
| `surface.content` | Opaque route/detail content; secondary surface within the base on iOS, content/control background on macOS |
| `surface.elevated` | Foreground detail panel when presented above content; resolve elevation separately on iOS |
| `text.primary` | Route names, status phrases, disruption instructions; primary label semantics |
| `text.secondary` | Supporting timestamp/source metadata; secondary label semantics, never disabled text |
| `status.disrupted` | Warning triangle with exclamation mark; phrase “Service disrupted” stays primary text |
| `status.normal` | Circle with check mark; phrase “Normal service” stays primary text |
| `status.unknown` | Diamond with question mark; phrase “Status unavailable” stays primary text |
| `selection.fill/text` | Paired selected-content roles; fallback uses `surface.selected` and `text.primary` |
| `selection.marker` | Leading rule and “Selected” use selected text role; never a warning tint |
| `interaction.accent` | Actual links and focus treatment only; platform focus role/user accent on Mac |
| `separator` | Decorative dividers only; not needed to identify rows or selection |

Symbols are framework-independent vector shapes, not a dependency on SF Symbols or emoji. Their status text remains visible even if symbols cannot render. Route-brand colors, if introduced, must stay separate from service status.

### Explicit fallback palette

These are proposed custom opaque sRGB colors, not Apple system values. Columns are `(appearance, Increase Contrast)`. Use the palette when no reliable semantic-color adapter exists. `surface.elevated = surface.content` in this flat fallback; an elevated panel additionally has a solid `text.secondary` boundary. All content text is on content, elevated, or selected surfaces, not directly on the dashboard base.

| Role | Light, off | Dark, off | Light, on | Dark, on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `surface.base` | #F4F5F7 | #10151C | #FFFFFF | #000000 |
| `surface.content` | #FFFFFF | #1C2530 | #FFFFFF | #080C10 |
| `surface.selected` | #E8EDF5 | #29384A | #E3E8EF | #162230 |
| `text.primary` | #17212B | #F1F5F9 | #000000 | #FFFFFF |
| `text.secondary` / `status.unknown` | #475569 | #CBD5E1 | #1F2937 | #E2E8F0 |
| `status.disrupted` | #9F1239 | #FDA4AF | #7F1231 | #FFC0CB |
| `status.normal` | #166534 | #86EFAC | #14532D | #B9F6CA |
| `interaction.accent` | #1D4ED8 | #93C5FD | #153EAB | #BFDBFE |

Keep status glyphs on an opaque content-colored patch inside selected rows, including with a native selection fill. This prevents the status color from colliding with an arbitrary user-selected accent. Selection text must use the foreground paired with the actual selection fill. Do not assume fallback foregrounds work on a native accent fill.

Reduce Transparency leaves the opaque fallback unchanged. Increase Contrast selects its column independently of appearance. Do not lower opacity for metadata, unknown status, hover, or an inactive window. Inactive native selection may use the platform’s paired unemphasized selection roles; retain “Selected” and the marker. Decorative separators may use `text.secondary` at full opacity or be omitted.

## Interaction and state contract

Each route row has stable identity, route name, status phrase/symbol, optional supporting summary, and a selection slot. The complete row is one selectable target. Status symbols are not extra controls. Reading order is route name, status, summary, selection state. Supply an accessible route name, current status, and selected state; omit duplicate decorative symbol descriptions.

```text
state = {selectedRouteId, focusedRouteId, routes, appearance, contrast, transparency}

render(row):
  selected = row.id == selectedRouteId
  surface = selected ? selection.fill : surface.content
  show route name and status phrase using the paired readable text role
  show status glyph using status[row.status] on opaque surface.content
  if selected: show leading rule and visible "Selected"
  if focused: show separate outer focus outline with an opaque backing gap

on row activation (tap, click, keyboard or assistive activation):
  selectedRouteId = row.id
  show that route'"'s detail content and persistent service status
  preserve the route's status; selection does not rewrite its color or meaning

on service update:
  update status phrase, glyph, summary and details together
  retain selectedRouteId and focusedRouteId
  do not infer \"Normal service\" from missing or failed data

on appearance / contrast / transparency / user-accent change:
  resolve all role pairs atomically, including open detail surfaces
  retain route selection, focused item, details and scroll position
"'```

Do not turn a service update into an automatic selection or navigation event. Unknown status includes a plain-language explanation if provided; a last-known timestamp is supporting information, not evidence of current normal service. Freshness thresholds require a separate data contract.

This is a preservation requirement, not a new typography system. [Accessibility — Vision and Speech](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility).

## Worked before → after

Illustrative route: **Route A**, currently disrupted and selected.

**Before:** White row, light gray “Route A,” red dot; selecting makes the red slightly darker. Without hue discrimination, neither disruption nor selection is reliably identifiable. Its contrast ratio is unknown.

**After, light fallback:** Selected fill #E8EDF5, primary text #17212B, leading primary-colored rule and visible “Selected.” The status reads **“Service disrupted — replacement buses between Central and Park.”** A #9F1239 warning triangle sits on a #FFFFFF opaque patch. Status and selection are independently readable in monochrome.

**After switching to dark while selected:** Fill becomes #29384A and text #F1F5F9; triangle becomes #FDA4AF on #1C2530. The same route and details remain selected. If focus moves to Route B, only its focus outline moves; Route A retains “Selected.” If Route A returns to normal service, its symbol and phrase change to “Normal service,” while its selection marker remains.

## Acceptance checks and observed results

Project thresholds: require at least 4.5:1 for all essential text and status glyphs; aim for 7:1 for custom text, especially small text. Require at least 3:1 for focus/selection boundaries against their adjacent backing. These conservative project gates do not claim full accessibility conformance. The local Accessibility guide gives its scoped Inspector table (up to 17 pt all weights: 4.5:1; 18 pt all weights and bold at any size: 3:1); the Dark Mode guide gives 4.5:1 and a custom-color aim of 7:1. This design chooses the stricter common floor rather than exploiting the lower text allowances. [Dark Mode — Colors](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/dark-mode#Dark-Mode-colors), [Accessibility — Vision](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility#Vision).

**Passed — specification/static calculation only:**

- All three service states have persistent text plus distinct shapes. Selection has its own text/marker; no essential state relies on hue alone.
- Four explicit fallback variants and live preference transitions are specified.
- A local Python 3 calculation used opaque sRGB inputs in the palette table: linearize each component with the standard 0.04045 breakpoint, compute luminance with weights 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722, and ratio `(lighter + .05)/(darker + .05)`. Results below are rounded; gates used the underlying values. Each cell is contrast on content / selected surface.

| Foreground | Light | Dark | Light increased | Dark increased |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Primary | 16.29 / 13.86 | 14.13 / 10.90 | 21.00 / 17.06 | 19.62 / 16.08 |
| Secondary / unknown | 7.58 / 6.45 | 10.43 / 8.04 | 14.68 / 11.92 | 15.91 / 13.05 |
| Disrupted | 8.02 / 6.82 | 8.19 / 6.31 | 10.33 / 8.39 | 12.76 / 10.46 |
| Normal | 7.13 / 6.07 | 11.02 / 8.50 | 9.11 / 7.40 | 15.97 / 13.10 |
| Accent | 6.70 / 5.70 | 8.58 / 6.62 | 9.09 / 7.39 | 13.81 / 11.32 |

**Failed / limits found:** The supplied design fails the non-color status requirement by description. The proposed default secondary text on a light selected row is 6.45:1, below the 7:1 aspiration but above the 4.5:1 gate; use primary text for essential disruption instructions. Accent-colored link text also misses that aspiration in some default cases; keep it for actual interactions. No runtime failure was established.

**Not executed — implementation acceptance gates:**

- Render iOS and macOS in light/dark × Increase Contrast off/on × Reduce Transparency off/on. All essential text, symbols, focus and selection cues must meet their actual composited pair thresholds; inspect resting and scrolled content. Recalculate native semantic/accent pairs independently of fallback measurements.
- Change system appearance and preferences with a selected row and open details. No light-only element, lost selection/focus, scroll jump, or merged elevated panel may remain.
- Test macOS user accents and active/inactive windows. Status must retain its meaning, selection text must use its paired foreground, and focus must remain separately visible.
- View without color and at 200% text size: identify normal, disrupted, unknown, selected and focused states; complete route selection and read details with no clipped essential content.
- Test touch/pointer, keyboard and supported assistive activation. Focus must reach each route; activation must open the correct details. Verify actual accessible names, state exposure and reading order with the relevant Apple tools, including VoiceOver; this document does not establish them.
- Test physical displays, bright/dim environments and relevant display profiles. Confirm symbol outlines and opaque patches remain legible rather than relying on numeric contrast alone.

## Evidence limits and audit trail

Only supplied local files and installed instructions were used. No web browsing occurred; official URLs above identify source articles recorded by the local package, not independently checked pages. The package labels its sources as a dated 2026-10-25 snapshot and does not establish independent review merely through file presence.

Read order, each through its installed path: root `apple-hig/SKILL.md`; project `interface.md`; `subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md`; that family'"'s "'`.topics/apple-hig-color/SKILL.md`, `.topics/apple-hig-dark-mode/SKILL.md`, `.topics/apple-hig-accessibility/SKILL.md`; then its `references/color.md`, `references/dark-mode.md`, `references/accessibility.md`. Each file was read by a separate `cat` command. All skill paths resolve under this project'"'s "'`.agents/skills/apple-hig/`.

This is a revised design contract, not a working dashboard. The contrast calculation validates only proposed opaque fallback pairs, not native rendering, antialiasing, transparency, desktop tinting, or the original palette. No Apple device, SDK compilation, GUI, Accessibility Inspector or assistive-technology execution occurred. Native semantic mapping and behavioral acceptance remain implementation work; no API availability or platform feasibility beyond this specification is asserted.
EOF'

  retain route selection, focused item, details and scroll position
"'```

Use ordinary platform selection/navigation behavior for the eventual container. Focus alone never selects a route. A focused unselected route must remain distinguishable from the selected route. Do not turn a service update into an automatic selection or navigation event. Unknown status includes a plain-language explanation if provided; a last-known timestamp is supporting information, not evidence of current normal service. Freshness thresholds require a separate data contract.

At 200% text enlargement, wrap status phrases and “Selected” onto additional lines rather than replacing them with dots or clipping them. This is a preservation requirement, not a new typography system. [Accessibility — Vision and Speech](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility).

## Worked before → after

Illustrative route: **Route A**, currently disrupted and selected.

**Before:** White row, light gray “Route A,” red dot; selecting makes the red slightly darker. Without hue discrimination, neither disruption nor selection is reliably identifiable. Its contrast ratio is unknown.

**After, light fallback:** Selected fill #E8EDF5, primary text #17212B, leading primary-colored rule and visible “Selected.” The status reads **“Service disrupted — replacement buses between Central and Park.”** A #9F1239 warning triangle sits on a #FFFFFF opaque patch. Status and selection are independently readable in monochrome.

**After switching to dark while selected:** Fill becomes #29384A and text #F1F5F9; triangle becomes #FDA4AF on #1C2530. The same route and details remain selected. If focus moves to Route B, only its focus outline moves; Route A retains “Selected.” If Route A returns to normal service, its symbol and phrase change to “Normal service,” while its selection marker remains.

## Acceptance checks and observed results

Project thresholds: require at least 4.5:1 for all essential text and status glyphs; aim for 7:1 for custom text, especially small text. Require at least 3:1 for focus/selection boundaries against their adjacent backing. These conservative project gates do not claim full accessibility conformance. The local Accessibility guide gives its scoped Inspector table (up to 17 pt all weights: 4.5:1; 18 pt all weights and bold at any size: 3:1); the Dark Mode guide gives 4.5:1 and a custom-color aim of 7:1. This design chooses the stricter common floor rather than exploiting the lower text allowances. [Dark Mode — Colors](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/dark-mode#Dark-Mode-colors), [Accessibility — Vision](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility#Vision).

**Passed — specification/static calculation only:**

- All three service states have persistent text plus distinct shapes. Selection has its own text/marker; no essential state relies on hue alone.
- Four explicit fallback variants and live preference transitions are specified.
- A local Python 3 calculation used opaque sRGB inputs in the palette table: linearize each component with the standard 0.04045 breakpoint, compute luminance with weights 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722, and ratio `(lighter + .05)/(darker + .05)`. Results below are rounded; gates used the underlying values. Each cell is contrast on content / selected surface.

| Foreground | Light | Dark | Light increased | Dark increased |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Primary | 16.29 / 13.86 | 14.13 / 10.90 | 21.00 / 17.06 | 19.62 / 16.08 |
| Secondary / unknown | 7.58 / 6.45 | 10.43 / 8.04 | 14.68 / 11.92 | 15.91 / 13.05 |
| Disrupted | 8.02 / 6.82 | 8.19 / 6.31 | 10.33 / 8.39 | 12.76 / 10.46 |
| Normal | 7.13 / 6.07 | 11.02 / 8.50 | 9.11 / 7.40 | 15.97 / 13.10 |
| Accent | 6.70 / 5.70 | 8.58 / 6.62 | 9.09 / 7.39 | 13.81 / 11.32 |

**Failed / limits found:** The supplied design fails the non-color status requirement by description. The proposed default secondary text on a light selected row is 6.45:1, below the 7:1 aspiration but above the 4.5:1 gate; use primary text for essential disruption instructions. Accent-colored link text also misses that aspiration in some default cases; keep it for actual interactions. No runtime failure was established.

**Not executed — implementation acceptance gates:**

- Render iOS and macOS in light/dark × Increase Contrast off/on × Reduce Transparency off/on. All essential text, symbols, focus and selection cues must meet their actual composited pair thresholds; inspect resting and scrolled content. Recalculate native semantic/accent pairs independently of fallback measurements.
- Change system appearance and preferences with a selected row and open details. No light-only element, lost selection/focus, scroll jump, or merged elevated panel may remain.
- Test macOS user accents and active/inactive windows. Status must retain its meaning, selection text must use its paired foreground, and focus must remain separately visible.
- View without color and at 200% text size: identify normal, disrupted, unknown, selected and focused states; complete route selection and read details with no clipped essential content.
- Test touch/pointer, keyboard and supported assistive activation. Focus must reach each route; activation must open the correct details. Verify actual accessible names, state exposure and reading order with the relevant Apple tools, including VoiceOver; this document does not establish them.
- Test physical displays, bright/dim environments and relevant display profiles. Confirm symbol outlines and opaque patches remain legible rather than relying on numeric contrast alone.

Only supplied local files and installed instructions were used. No web browsing occurred; official URLs above identify source articles recorded by the local package, not independently checked pages.
